comments.body:
Implementation done in worktree ../reopen-parent-cascade (branch reopen-parent-cascade), TDD RED-first.

RED: added 7 reopen cases to tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_claim_transition_parent_cascade.py; 4 failed against unpatched code (closed parent stayed closed on reopen; multi-level chain not cascaded; raced parent DID NOT RAISE; CLI parity), 3 passed trivially (the no-op parent cases).

GREEN: generalized the existing cascade seam instead of adding a second one.
- _resolve_open_parent -> new _resolve_parent_in_status(tracker, ticket_id, status); _resolve_open_parent is now its 'open' specialization, so claim.py is untouched.
- _cascade_open_parent -> _cascade_parent_first, driven by a module-level _CASCADING_EDGES table mapping the child's (current, target) edge to the parent status eligible on it: ('open','in_progress') -> 'open' (unchanged) and ('closed','open') -> 'closed' (the fix). The parent moves along the SAME edge, ahead of the child, under the existing _cascade_seen cycle guard and the existing fail-fast error wrapping (message names the parent; ConcurrencyMismatch identity/exit 10 preserved).
- Stale symbol references updated per the plan-review advisory: the transition.py call-site comment and the transition_close.py module docstring.
- reopen docstring (_lib_writes.py) and docs/concurrency.md I4a updated; I4a now tables both cascading edges and explains why the close-time open-children guard's asymmetry made this edge necessary.

Semantics note on AC1's word 'atomic': delivered as the documented claim/transition cascade shape it is asked to mirror - one user-visible invocation, sequential and fail-fast, NOT transactional (no rollback if the parent succeeds and the child then fails). That is docs/concurrency.md I4a's existing contract; making reopen transactional would have been a different, larger change to the shared seam.

Scope note: transition_close.py (one-word docstring cross-reference) was added to file_impact after the fact.

Gates locally green: make lint (incl. complexity ratchet new=0 increased=0 stale=0), make typecheck, and tests/interfaces/lifecycle + tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py = 513 passed. transition.py is 741 LOC, under the 800 cap.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Landed: Gerrit change 1915 merged as ed864a9726 on origin/main (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, no unresolved comments). Change 1921 was an accidental duplicate created when an amend dropped the Change-Id; abandoned.

Two review rounds beyond the first push:

1) Patchset 1 CI failure (Verified -1) on tests/interfaces/store/test_completion_verifier.py::test_child_closure_does_not_recurse_grandchildren, deterministic across ubuntu py3.11/3.12/3.13 and macos py3.13. Root cause: NOT a cascade defect. That test manufactures a 'closed direct child with an open grandchild' state by reopening the grandchild AFTER its ancestors closed - which is precisely the invalid state this bug exists to prevent. The child 'C' it reports as open is the reopened grandchild's DIRECT parent, so the cascade reopening it is correct behavior; the fix dissolved the fixture's precondition. Repaired by rebuilding the state with the documented cascade=False replay seam (NDJSON-import path), leaving the test's subject and its assertion byte-identical, plus a new explicit assertion that the child stays closed. The state remains reachable in the field via an offline clone's merge or an import replay, so the verifier's non-recursion still has to hold and is still what the test proves.

2) LLM-Review advisory on _cascade_parent_first aborting the child on ANY parent CommandError, unlike claim_compute. Adopted: the cascade now carries claim_compute's TOCTOU benign-race re-check. The cascade decision reads the parent status without the write lock, so a peer can move it in between; on a parent failure the parent's live status is re-checked and an already-moved parent is benign (child proceeds), while a parent still genuinely in the eligible status still aborts the child with the exit-code-preserving error. This does loosen the pre-existing open -> in_progress failure path - stated explicitly in the plan rather than slipped in - and brings the two cascades into agreement. Two new tests cover the benign race on both edges. claim's own cascade is untouched.

Final shape: 6 files, +333/-81. tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_claim_transition_parent_cascade.py is 25/25 green, test_completion_verifier.py 23/23 green, make lint (complexity ratchet new=0 increased=0 stale=0) and make typecheck clean, transition.py 741 LOC under the 800 cap.

Follow-up filed: paragonite-fruited-minnow (96db-365e-f2c3-4547), linked discovered_from - the closed -> in_progress reactivation edge still lacks the cascade and can leave the same invalid state; deliberately excluded here because cascading a parent from closed straight to in_progress drags it through its own plan-review start-work gate, which deserves its own review.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
`rebar reopen <child>` moves a closed ticket to open but does NOT cascade to its
still-closed parent(s). `reopen` is a thin delegation to
`transition(ticket_id, "closed", "open")` (`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:430`; CLI
`reopen_cli` at `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:689`), and the parent-first cascade in
`transition_compute` fires only on the `open -> in_progress` edge (`_cascade_open_parent`,
defined at `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:387`, called from `transition_compute` at
`src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:341`). The close-time guard only blocks CLOSING a
parent that has open children, so nothing catches the other direction: the store can hold
a CLOSED parent with an OPEN/in_progress child.

Observed while closing epic e215-ab23-ed6a-4791: after the epic returned to `closed`,
reopening child stories aabf-d89e-d05a-45c4 and 075b-1479-dcb7-40ab left the epic `closed`
while the children were `in_progress`.

## Approach
Generalize the existing cascade seam rather than adding a second parallel one, so both
edges keep one implementation, one error shape, and one cycle guard.

1. Add `_resolve_parent_in_status(tracker, ticket_id, status)` beside
   `_resolve_open_parent` (`src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:93`), which today hardcodes
   the `"open"` comparison. `_resolve_open_parent` becomes a one-line delegation, so its
   other caller (`src/rebar/_commands/claim.py:190,193,215`) needs no edit.
2. Replace `_cascade_open_parent` with an edge-table-driven `_cascade_parent_first`: a
   module-level map from `(current_status, target_status)` to the eligible parent status —
   `("open", "in_progress") -> "open"` (today's behavior, unchanged) and
   `("closed", "open") -> "closed"` (the fix). The parent transitions on the SAME edge
   before the child, recursing up the chain under the existing `_cascade_seen` cycle guard
   with the existing fail-fast wrapping that names the parent and preserves
   `ConcurrencyMismatch` (exit 10). Update the call site at
   `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:341` and the stale references to the old name: the
   comment above that call site and the `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:13`
   module docstring.
3. Close the cascade's TOCTOU asymmetry with `claim`. The cascade DECISION reads the
   parent's status without the write lock, so a peer can move it in between.
   `claim_compute` already re-checks the parent's live status on a parent failure and
   treats an already-moved parent as benign (`src/rebar/_commands/claim.py:215`);
   `_cascade_open_parent` does not, so a benign race aborts the child. Give
   `_cascade_parent_first` the same re-check. This DOES loosen the existing
   `open -> in_progress` failure path (a benign race lets the child through instead of
   aborting) — intended parity with `claim`, and only where the cascade's purpose was
   already satisfied.
4. Update the `reopen` docstring (`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:430`), the
   `transition_compute` docstring, and `docs/concurrency.md` §I4a, which currently states
   that `close`/`reopen`/`blocked` never cascade.
5. Repair `test_child_closure_does_not_recurse_grandchildren` in
   `tests/interfaces/store/test_completion_verifier.py`. It manufactures a
   closed-child-with-open-grandchild state by reopening the grandchild after its ancestors
   closed — exactly the invalid state this bug is about — so the new cascade dissolves its
   precondition. Rebuild that state with the documented `cascade=False` replay seam (still
   reachable in the field via an offline clone's merge or an NDJSON import), leaving the
   test's subject and assertion untouched.

Why this fits: the invariant restored here ("a parent is never more closed than its
children") is symmetric with the one `open -> in_progress` already enforces, and the
existing helper already carries the fail-fast, exit-code-preserving, cycle-guarded
semantics this edge needs. A separate copy would be a second place to drift.

Semantics deliberately MIRROR the documented cascade (`docs/concurrency.md` §I4a): one
invocation, sequential and fail-fast, NOT transactional — a genuine parent failure aborts
the child preserving its exit code, and a parent that succeeded before a child failure is
not rolled back. Only `closed -> open` is ADDED to the edge table; `* -> closed` keeps its
non-cascading behavior and its open-children guard, and a parent that is
`in_progress`/`blocked`/`open`/absent is not cascaded.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py` — add `_resolve_parent_in_status`, reduce
  `_resolve_open_parent` to a delegation, replace `_cascade_open_parent` with
  `_cascade_parent_first` plus the benign-race re-check, update call site and docstrings.
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — refresh the module docstring's reference to
  the renamed helper.
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` — document the reopen cascade on `reopen`.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_claim_transition_parent_cascade.py` — reopen-cascade
  and benign-race cases beside the existing claim/transition cases.
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_completion_verifier.py` — rebuild the non-recursion test's
  fixture state with `cascade=False`.
- `docs/concurrency.md` — §I4a: both cascading edges and the benign-race re-check.

Assume the no-rollback half of the fail-fast contract is correct and is not revisited here.

## Testing
Held-out tests in `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_claim_transition_parent_cascade.py`,
using that file's existing `rebar_repo` fixture and `_status()` helper:
- Happy path: reopen a closed child under a closed parent -> both `open`.
- No-op: reopen a closed child whose parent is already `open` (and, separately, already
  `in_progress`) -> the parent's status is untouched.
- Multi-level: a closed grand/parent/child chain, reopen the leaf -> all three `open`.
- Failure/edge: monkeypatch `txn.transition_core` to raise `ConcurrencyMismatch` for the
  parent -> `rebar.reopen(child)` raises `ConcurrencyError` with `returncode == 10`, the
  message names the parent, and the child is still `closed` (no partial cascade).
- Benign race, both edges: monkeypatch `txn.transition_core` so the parent LEAVES the
  eligible status and then raises -> the child still moves and the peer's write stands.
- `cascade=False` suppression on the reopen edge.
- Regression: `test_close_does_not_cascade_to_parent` keeps passing, and
  `tests/interfaces/store/test_completion_verifier.py` passes.
Run: `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_claim_transition_parent_cascade.py
tests/interfaces/store/test_completion_verifier.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Reopening a child under a closed parent reopens that parent transitively to the
      root, in one invocation, parent before child. Checked by the happy-path and
      multi-level tests asserting every ancestor is `open` after one `rebar.reopen(leaf)`.
- [x] No closed parent is left holding a non-closed child after a reopen. Checked by the
      happy-path and multi-level tests asserting the parent is `open`, not `closed`.
- [x] An already-`open` or already-`in_progress` parent is not disturbed by a reopen.
      Checked by the two no-op tests.
- [x] A raced parent surfaces `ConcurrencyError`/exit 10 naming the parent, with the child
      left `closed`. Checked by the failure/edge test.
- [x] The transition cascade treats a benign parent race exactly as `claim`'s cascade
      does. Checked by the two benign-race tests asserting the child still moves.
- [x] `docs/concurrency.md` §I4a describes the `closed -> open` cascade beside the
      `open -> in_progress` one and no longer says `reopen` never cascades. Checked by
      reading the updated §I4a.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass, complexity ratchet reporting no `new` or
      `increased` entries.
